'''How Did We Get Into This Mess?''' is a [[Light]] [[Interrupt]] from [[Premiere (Japanese)|Premiere (Japanese)]].

Title

一体全体どうして、こんな羽目になるのかね

Card Text

自分のドロイドが「大砂原」もしくは「アクセス・リンク」のある位置にいる時に使う。１フォース消費して、手札を全部ユーズドデッキに捨てる。同じ枚数のカードをリザーブデッキから引いて手札にする。ドロイドがＣ－３ＰＯかＲ２－Ｄ２ならば、引くカードの枚数に１枚足せる。

Lore

''大砂原に不時着した後、Ｒ２－Ｄ２は人間の居住区のありそうな峡谷へ向かうと主張した。Ｃ－３ＰＯは、反対だった。''

Translation of Japanese Text

'''Title:''' How on earth did we get into this situation? '''Card text:''' Use when your droid is at the ‘Great Desert’ or a location with an ‘access link.’ Spend 1 Force to discard your entire hand to the Used Pile. Draw the same number of cards from the Reserve Deck into your hand. If the droid is C-3PO or R2-D2, you may add one to the number of cards drawn. '''Lore:''' After making an emergency landing in the great desert, R2-D2 insisted on heading toward a canyon likely to contain human settlements. C-3PO disagreed. '''Comparison with the English printing:''' The Japanese uses ‘Great Desert’ for the location called the Dune Sea in English and ‘access link’ where the English says Scomp link. The Japanese says one card may be added to the draw if the droid is C-3PO or R2-D2; the English says to draw one extra card.

Notes

Japanese-language printing of [[How Did We Get Into This Mess?]] in [[Premiere (Japanese)]].[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2], p. 97. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192828/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf Internet Archive].[https://www.psacard.com/psasetregistry/showcase/miscellaneous/star-wars-ccg-japanese-premiere/imagegallery/29544 Japanese Premiere collector image gallery], PSA.

Title

反乱軍兵員

Card Text

能力値＞２を持つ反乱軍と同じ位置カードに配備する場合、配備コストなし。

Lore

''コレリアン・コルベットの兵士、オルデラン出身のチャド・ヒルズ少尉は、打倒帝国に生涯を捧げた忠実なる反乱軍志願兵の代表的人物といえる。宇宙船内及び地上戦闘技術を持つ。''

Translation of Japanese Text

'''Title:''' Rebel personnel. '''Card text:''' Deploys at no deploy cost when deployed to the same location card as a Rebel with ability greater than 2. '''Lore:''' Corellian Corvette soldier Ensign Chad Hilse, from Alderaan, exemplifies the loyal Rebel volunteers who have devoted their lives to defeating the Empire. He has skills in combat aboard starships and on the ground. '''Comparison with the English printing:''' The Japanese says the same location card as a Rebel with ability greater than 2. The English says the same site as one of your Rebels with ability greater than 2.

Notes

Japanese-language printing of [[Rebel Trooper]] in [[Premiere (Japanese)]].[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2], p. 97. Title

サイトア・カルファス

Card Text

戦士ではないキャラクター（ドロイドを除く）に配備すると、戦士技能［戦士アイコン］を与える。または戦士に配備すると、戦闘力＋１（「意識操作」カードの影響を受けない）。

Lore

''惑星ダークティル出身のサウリンの女性。同族のドロイド商人ハーチェクのボディーガード。サイトアは、それに見合うと判断した者に、戦闘技能を教える。''

Translation of Japanese Text

'''Title:''' Sai'torr Kal Fas. '''Card text:''' Deploy on a non-warrior character (except a droid) to give that character warrior skill. Or deploy on a warrior for power +1. (Not affected by the ‘Mind Manipulation’ card.) '''Lore:''' A Saurin woman from the planet Durkteel and bodyguard to the Saurin droid merchant Hrchek. Sai'torr teaches combat skills to those she judges worthy. '''Comparison with the English printing:''' The Japanese says she teaches those she judges worthy; the English says those who prove themselves worthy. The Japanese names 意識操作 where the English printing names Alter.

Notes

Japanese-language printing of [[Sai'torr Kal Fas]] in [[Premiere (Japanese)]].[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2], p. 97. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192828/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf Internet Archive].[https://www.psacard.com/psasetregistry/showcase/miscellaneous/star-wars-ccg-japanese-premiere/imagegallery/29544 Japanese Premiere collector image gallery], PSA.

Title

ハンのサイコロ

Card Text

戦闘で、戦闘運命数を引いた時に使う。自分の能力値２以上のキャラクターが参加していないと使えない。１フォース消費して、引いた戦闘運命数をキャンセルし、新しい戦闘運命数を引ける。

Lore

''ミレニアム・ファルコンのコクピットには、お守りに一組のサイコロが吊してある。「全てを操る万能なるフォースなんてものには、お目にかかったことがねえ。」''

Translation of Japanese Text

'''Title:''' Han's dice. '''Card text:''' Use when a battle destiny is drawn in battle. You cannot use it unless one of your characters with ability 2 or more is participating. Spend 1 Force to cancel the battle destiny just drawn and draw a new battle destiny. '''Lore:''' A pair of dice hangs in the Millennium Falcon's cockpit as a good-luck charm. ‘I've never encountered an all-powerful Force that controls everything.’ '''Comparison with the English printing:''' The Japanese requires one of your participating characters to have ability 2 or more; the English requires ability greater than 2. The Japanese says to cancel the drawn battle destiny and draw a new one; the English says to draw another instead of the one just drawn.

Notes

Japanese-language printing of [[Han's Dice]] in [[Premiere (Japanese)]].[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2], p. 97. Title

オーガナ家の式典用ネックレス

Card Text

任意のヤヴィン４の位置カードに配備する。帝国軍カードを１つ対象に選ぶ。このカードと同じ位置に着けば、ネックレスを“盗んだ”ことになる。以後、ネックレスがある位置では、フォース消耗を＋１できる。さらに、隣接している位置カードを支配していれば、そこへコストなしで移動させ、フォース消耗に＋１できる。以降、繰り返し。

Lore

''レイア姫がヤヴィンの戦勝祝典でつけていたネックレス。オルデランの統治者に何十世代も伝わる力を秘めた工芸品。''

Translation of Japanese Text

'''Title:''' The Organa family's ceremonial necklace. '''Card text:''' Deploy on any Yavin 4 location card. Choose an Imperial card as the target. When it reaches the same location as this card, the necklace is ‘stolen.’ Thereafter, at the location where the necklace is, you may add 1 to the Force drain. In addition, if you control an adjacent location card, you may move it there at no cost and add 1 to the Force drain. Repeat thereafter. '''Lore:''' The necklace Princess Leia wore at the Yavin victory celebration. A crafted object with hidden power, passed down among Alderaan's rulers for dozens of generations. '''Comparison with the English printing:''' The Japanese refers to a Yavin 4 location card and an Imperial card; the English specifies a Yavin 4 site and targets an Imperial. The Japanese says the drain may be increased at the necklace's location and describes moving it to an adjacent controlled location; the English describes passing it to an adjacent controlled site during Force drains.

Notes

Japanese-language printing of [[Organa's Ceremonial Necklace]] in [[Premiere (Japanese)]].[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2], p. 97. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192828/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf Internet Archive].[https://www.psacard.com/psasetregistry/showcase/miscellaneous/star-wars-ccg-japanese-premiere/imagegallery/29544 Japanese Premiere collector image gallery], PSA.

Title

ガダフィの杖

Card Text

２フォース消費して、タスケン・レイダーに配備する。起動にフォースを必要としない。その場で戦闘が始まった場合、即座に運命数を２枚引く。２枚の運命数の合計＞５ならば、敵は武器を“はじき飛ばされて”、この戦闘では使えなくなる。

Lore

''“ガッフィ”とも呼ばれる、タスケン・レイダーの好む武器。廃棄された金属などで作られる。相手を脅し、恐怖させるに十分な武器である。''

Translation of Japanese Text

'''Title:''' Gaderffii staff. '''Card text:''' Spend 2 Force to deploy on a Tusken Raider. No Force is required to activate it. If a battle begins there, immediately draw two destiny. If their total is greater than 5, the enemy's weapons are ‘knocked away’ and cannot be used in this battle. '''Lore:''' A weapon favored by Tusken Raiders, also called a ‘gaffi.’ Made from discarded metal and similar materials, it is sufficient to threaten and frighten an opponent. '''Comparison with the English printing:''' The Japanese says activating it requires no Force; the English says it may target for free. The Japanese describes a battle beginning there, while the English says a battle has just been initiated where the weapon is present.

Notes

Japanese-language printing of [[Gaderffii Stick]] in [[Premiere (Japanese)]].[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2], p. 97. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192828/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf Internet Archive].[https://www.psacard.com/psasetregistry/showcase/miscellaneous/star-wars-ccg-japanese-premiere/imagegallery/29544 Japanese Premiere collector image gallery], PSA.

Title

ケット・マリス

Card Text

どちらかを選ぶ。１：戦士技能を持たないキャラクターに配備して（ドロイドは除く）、戦士［戦士アイコン］技能を持たせる。２：戦士キャラクターに配備して、戦闘力＋１とする。（「意識操作」の効果を受けない）

Lore

''ジャバ・ザ・ハットやギャング達は、暗殺者を重用する。プリンス・シゾールの“シャドウ・キラー”である彼は、モス・アイズリーで血生臭い秘密任務についている。''

Translation of Japanese Text

'''Title:''' Ket Maliss. '''Card text:''' Choose one. 1: Deploy on a character without warrior skill, excluding droids, and give that character warrior skill. 2: Deploy on a warrior character and make its power +1. (Not affected by ‘Mind Manipulation.’) '''Lore:''' Jabba the Hutt and other gangsters place great value on assassins. Prince Xizor's ‘shadow killer’ is on a bloody secret mission in Mos Eisley. '''Comparison with the English printing:''' The Japanese lore calls the mission bloody and secret; the English calls his business unknown but undoubtedly lethal. The Japanese numbers the two deployment options and uses 意識操作 for the card named Alter in the English printing.

Notes

Japanese-language printing of [[Ket Maliss]] in [[Premiere (Japanese)]].[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2], p. 97. Title

メーカーに感謝

Card Text

相手の支配フェイズ、５フォース以上の消耗を受け、なおかつ、場に自分のドロイドがいる場合に、１フォース消費して使用できる。運命数を引く。その数の分だけロストデッキからランダムに選んで再使用してよい。

Lore

''ドロイドにとって、“創りしもの”への情熱は、神や宗教に匹敵する存在である。Ｃ－３ＰＯは、待望のオイルバスにありついた時、このフレーズを使った。''

Translation of Japanese Text

'''Title:''' Thank the Maker. '''Card text:''' During the opponent's control phase, if you have suffered a drain of 5 or more Force and have your droid on the table, you may spend 1 Force to use this. Draw destiny. You may randomly select that number from the Lost Pile and reuse them. '''Lore:''' For droids, devotion to ‘the one who creates’ is comparable to God or religion. C-3PO used this phrase when he obtained a long-awaited oil bath. '''Comparison with the English printing:''' The Japanese says the randomly selected cards may be reused, while the English says they are retrieved from the Lost Pile. The Japanese lore calls the bath long-awaited; the English describes a much-needed cleansing oil bath.

Notes

Japanese-language printing of [[Thank The Maker]] in [[Premiere (Japanese)]].[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2], p. 97.
